title: Group Anagrams
prompt:
Given an array of lowercase words, group the words that are anagrams of each other (same letters, same counts, any order).

Write groupAnagrams(words). To make the answer predictable: return the groups in the order their first word appears in the input, and keep the words inside each group in input order.

  • groupAnagrams(['tea', 'eat', 'tan', 'ate', 'nat', 'bat']) → [['tea', 'eat', 'ate'], ['tan', 'nat'], ['bat']]
  • groupAnagrams(['']) → [['']]
  • groupAnagrams([]) → []

Constraints: up to 10^4 words, each up to 100 letters. Comparing every pair of words is too slow; aim for one pass with a Map.

tests.name: empty input and the empty word
duplicate words stay in the same group
same letters but different counts are NOT anagrams

hints: Trigger: anagram + group. That is the "group by a key" shape: a Map from key to an array of words.
Idea: the key must be identical for every anagram and different otherwise. Sorting the word's letters works: tea, eat and ate all become aet.

Code shape: const key = word.split('').sort().join(''); if (!groups.has(key)) groups.set(key, []); groups.get(key).push(word); then return [...groups.values()]. A Map remembers insertion order, which gives you the required group order for free.
explain:
Time O(n · k log k), space O(n · k) for n words of length up to k: each word is sorted once to build its key, and each map operation is O(1). The brute force compared every pair of words, O(n²) comparisons; a signature lets each word find its group on its own.

A faster key avoids sorting: count the 26 letters and use the counts as the key (for example '1#0#0#...'), giving O(n · k). Mention it as an optimization; the sorted key is clearer and usually fine.

How to say it: "Anagrams share the same sorted letters, so I'll use that as a key in a hash map from key to list of words. One pass, O(n · k log k)."
